newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BTP vol up, put trading dominates.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BTP vol up, put trading dominates.

text.p: Implied volatility of options on Italian BTPs traded on LIFFE rose sharply on Wednesday with put buying providing the main activity for the market, brokers said.
"Fear of the downside is generating these higher levels in puts. That is the big feature of today," said a broker at a French house in London.
Brokers quoted implied volatility for at-the-money September BTP options at 7.6 to 7.7 percent, having risen from 7.1 percent on Tuesday.
"The market seems to be well bid with only 14 days to go. We've seen good levels going through on puts," the broker said.
September options will expire on August 20.
He said a French brokerage had a been buyer of the 134.00 strike, while a British bank had bought the 134.50 puts.
By 1221 GMT, LIFFE data showed over 2,500 lots of 134.00 puts had been traded and over 2,400 lots at 134.50.

"The market is quite nervous so for the moment (volatility) will keep high, but it depends on events later in the week as to whether it continues to rise," said a trader at an Italian bank in London referring to the Bundesbank's concerns about the strength of the U.S. dollar against the mark.
"I don't think it will go much higher if the market settles down but for the moment we are waiting to see if the market moves in a more positive direction," he said.
The Italian bank trader said the activity this session had been mostly confined to the front month with options on December BTPs remaining quiet and implied volatility only slightly higher.
The underlying September BTP futures were at 135.53, up 0.38 on the day, having formed a low at 134.75 earlier in the session.
